Question B-003-002-002.

Why the correct answer is right: A microphone transduces changing air pressure from speech into an electrical audio signal.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "is quieter than AM or SSB microphones": Relative acoustic noise is not what makes a frequency-modulation (FM) microphone work. The transmitter needs the microphone to turn speech pressure into audio voltage.
- sourceIndex 2: "has a different tone than other microphones": Tone colour is a quality difference, not the basic transducer action needed at the first audio block.
- sourceIndex 3: "has a wider frequency range than other microphones": A wider audio response may change fidelity, but FM, amplitude modulation (AM), and single sideband (SSB) microphones all serve by converting speech sound into an electrical audio signal.
